messages:
emily: Hi team — first day! Upgraded to macOS 14.1 and completed Kandji enrollment, but corporate Wi-Fi (802.1x) keeps failing and Chrome/Safari complain the Redwood Root CA is untrusted. Keychain keeps prompting. Who should I ping for the CA/trust fix?
onboard-bot: Welcome to Redwood, @emily! :tada: IT usually handles cert pushes. Pinging them now.
it-support: Hey Emily, welcome — can you paste the output of `profiles status -type enrollment` and `sw_vers -productVersion`? Also does the device say "Enrolled via Kandji" in System Settings > Profiles?
emily: Paste below:
`$ profiles status -type enrollment
Enrolled via Kandji (MDM) — profile active`
`$ sw_vers -productVersion
14.1`
Yes it shows Kandji active. Wi-Fi connects but gets an authentication error and keychain prompts for Redwood Root CA whenever an app tries to load the cert.
ryan: Thanks — sounds like the company root CA didn't land in the System keychain as trusted during the upgrade. We can either push the cert via Kandji (recommended) or give you temp-admin for a quick manual trust. Which do you prefer?
emily: Would prefer Kandji push if that's faster and avoids running sudo. How long does that usually take?
ryan: If I push via Kandji it hits devices on the next policy check (usually within 5-10 minutes). If you're ok waiting, I'll queue it now. If you need immediate access, I can grant a 1-hour temp-admin so you can trust it manually while the policy propagates.
people-ops: Quick welcome from People Ops too :wave: — let us know if onboarding access (VPN, SSO) is blocked, we can expedite.
emily: I'll wait for the Kandji push. Thanks!
ryan: Pushing Redwood-Root-CA certificate via Kandji now. On my side I also verified Kandji has the "install certificate (system)" payload targeted to your serial.
emily: Got a notice to accept a system profile install and then a Keychain prompt — still seeing an untrusted cert on Safari though. Any additional steps?
ryan: Two quick checks: 1) try restarting Safari after the cert push, 2) confirm the cert is present in System keychain and set to "Always Trust". If it's not set to Always Trust we can update the payload to enforce trust. If you want the manual command (only if temp-admin granted): `sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain /path/to/redwood-root-ca.pem`
emily: No sudo yet, but after a restart Safari now loads internal sites fine. Looks like the policy applied but some apps needed a restart. Everything seems good. Thanks @ryan!
ryan: Awesome — closing the loop. If SSO or VPN still throw cert errors, tag #help or DM IT and we'll reprovision the cert with enforced trust. Welcome aboard and congrats on day one! :tada:
